question: Should this experimental cross-owner update flow merge with fail-closed `update_partial` plus manual status/Doctor recovery, or must it first provide a stronger reconcile/retry contract after live external-boundary proof?
rationale: Tests can validate local state transitions, but they cannot choose the product contract for an external installer, configuration writer, and Gateway scheduler that cannot share one transaction and may not return an authoritative mutation receipt.

options.title: Require live proof and accept the bounded contract
options.body: Require redacted real runs for package replacement, Gateway cron retry/convergence, and partial-state recovery, then explicitly approve `update_partial` plus status/Doctor and fresh-plan recovery as the experimental contract.

options.title: Narrow the first apply release
options.body: Defer package and Gateway mutation from this command until operation-identity reconciliation is available, retaining only owners with fully demonstrable rollback behavior.

options.title: Pause the apply slice
options.body: Keep the planner stack open but do not merge this mutation stage until the RFC settles the required recovery semantics.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and accept the bounded contract
recommendation.body: Require redacted real runs for package replacement, Gateway cron retry/convergence, and partial-state recovery, then explicitly approve `update_partial` plus status/Doctor and fresh-plan recovery as the experimental contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment identifies the unresolved external-boundary recovery criteria that need an explicit product and operational decision.
